checks.label: Whatever magnitude of DC voltage would produce the same amount of heat energy dissipation through an equal resistance is the DC equivalent: for every shape on both cards, the DC level where the bars match heats the equal resistance as much as the drawn power humps do on average

For a sine wave, the RMS value is approximately 0.707 of its peak value: on the heater test the bars match at 70.7 V of the 100 V peak, a ratio of 0.707, where the steady DC heater takes the AC heater's 500 W

UK mains voltage is 230 V RMS, so the peak voltage is about 325 V (230 × √2): on the mains card the wave reaches 325 V at the top of each cycle and −325 V at the bottom, and 230 V of DC heats the twin heater just as much, 1000 W
UK mains electricity operates at a nominal voltage of 230V: the mains card runs at 230 V rms, and its 1 kW heater is 230² ÷ 1000 = 52.9 Ω

Heat goes with the square, not the plain average: the 100 V sine averages 63.7 V over half a cycle, and 63.7 V of DC gives only about 406 W against 500 W, while a steady 100 V gives 1000 W, twice the AC heater's heat

Each shape has its own ratio: the triangle's humps average a third of their 1000 W top, 333 W, matching at 57.7 V, 0.577 of the peak, and the square's power is a flat 1000 W, matching at 100 V, a ratio of 1.000

The average-reading meter reads the folded wave's average marked up by 1.11, 0.707 ÷ 0.637: 230 V on the mains sine, 180 V on the 325 V triangle while the bars match at 188 V, 361 V on the 325 V square, and 111 V on the 100 V square
At every DC level from 0 V to 120 V the DC heater takes the level squared ÷ 10, the share of the peak is the level ÷ 100, and the bars show a match only at 70.7 V
Each puzzle accepts only its right answer; before an answer its picture hides what is asked (the DC level, the DC heat or the wave), and each wrong pick draws what it claims, in red
On every screen, each drawn point of the power humps is the drawn voltage at that moment squared ÷ the resistance
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
